page.overview:
What is Cyclizar?

Cyclizar overall resembles a reptilian creature, mostly with lizard attributes. Its body is primarily green, though black features also cover its body. Its hands and feet each have four fingers/toes, with the two innermost ones being together and the two outermost ones spreading out. Black sections of its body appear on its hands (which dot its palms and fingers), its tail (which is sectioned and has a white tip), and its head. The black section on its head also curves back, resembling a bicycle helmet, and goes down to its neck. An orange circular mark is also on its head, just near its eyes. A black plate can also be seen where its tail and body meet. Cyclizar also has a protrusion from its throat, resembling a bike tire. When Cyclizar is being ridden on, it puffs up this protrusion and curls its tail, making the appearance of wheels.

Cyclizar are overall quite mild Pokémon and do not mind the presence of humans, as they have worked together since Paldea's ancient times. They gladly allow human riders to climb on their back and use them as transportation; this is because a human’s body temperature can help regulate Cyclizar's body heat, keeping them warm and staving off cold temperatures.

Cyclizar are able to run at speeds of up to 70 miles per hour while carrying a human rider, making them great for human transportation in the Paldea region. Their sturdy head and tail help maintain stability, allowing them to absorb blows and shocks while in and out of battle.

Cyclizar's lizard-like attributes and throat protrusion appear to make it based on an , a family of lizards who typically have a colorful flap of skin on their throats for display. It also bears a resemblance to . Some elements of its design appear to be inspired by a or , as its throat and tail resemble tires. Its head also resembles the shape of a bicycle helmet, its cheeks are similar to turn signal lights, its rear looks like a motorcycle seat, and the protrusion on its chest together with its tail resemble rubber tires, the latter especially when curled.
